incident: Adding the 'Summer Olympics' topic, the live worksheetGenerator() shipped a math question -- 'China won 38 out of 250 games. What percent of their games did they win?' -- that asserted a false 'part of' relationship: wins+draws+losses (88) did not reconcile with the games field (250) in that topic's own data.
root_cause: generateWorksheet() called winPercentageQuestion() on a fixed array position for every topic, regardless of whether that topic's data actually supported the 'X out of Y games' framing winPercentageQuestion's prompt asserts. The safety-reviewer sub-agent had already flagged this exact data inconsistency, and question-writer had already independently avoided building a percentage question from it in its own draft -- but the shipped code never consulted that curated choice; it always ran the same three templates by position.
fix: Added winPercentageIsSound() as a guard in backend/src/worksheetGenerator.js: only call winPercentageQuestion() when wins+draws+losses reconciles with games; otherwise fall back to a second averageGoalsQuestion() (a ratio, not a 'part of' claim). The fallback independently reproduced exactly what question-writer had already chosen on its own.
lesson: A sub-agent's guardrail-respecting decision only protects the user if the code path that ships to production actually consults that decision. Draft-artifact evals (evals/run-all.mjs against evals/runs/<slug>/) couldn't see this bug because they never looked at what generateWorksheet() actually returns -- only checking the live, shipped output (now evals/shipped-worksheet.eval.mjs) caught it. See evals/runs/RUN-LOG.md for the full run log.
